recipes.name: Homemade Chicken Gravy
ingredients_raw: 1 quart cold chicken stock, or more if needed
salt and ground white pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Gradually whisk in flour, reduce heat to low, and stir until the roux has turned golden and smells like a cooked pie crust, 10 to 12 minutes.
Whisk in about 2 cups of cold stock, a little at a time, stirring to remove any lumps. Add remaining 2 cups stock.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until gravy is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, 10 to 15 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream, and season with salt, white pepper, and cayenne. Taste and if the gravy still tastes starchy, let it simmer a little longer, adding more cold stock if necessary.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Chicken Gravy
raw_recipe.description: Make chicken gravy from scratch with Chef John's recipe that starts with a basic roux and adds stock and cream, and you'll never buy packet gravy again!

video.description: Indulge in the rich and savory goodness of homemade chicken gravy with this tantalizing video tutorial! Join Chef John as he reveals the secrets behind creating a luscious, flavorful gravy that will take your chicken dishes to a whole new level. Whether you're preparing a Sunday roast or a weeknight chicken dinner, this video will equip you with the skills to master the art of homemade chicken gravy. Get ready to elevate your culinary creations!

review.reviewBody: OH BOY! This is REAL Chicken Gravy! Don't be afraid to cook your roux - if needs to be cooked slowly to a blonde stage - like Chef John says it will smell like pie crust. Good chicken stock makes a huge difference with this gravy. I did add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the roux along with some white pepper. Then proceeded as directed....taste tasted and added a bit more. Will I make again? You bet!
This recipe was delicious. I used half and half instead of heavy cream because I didn't have any.

I really enjoyed this recipe. I've never bought gravy mixes and have always tried my hand at homemade gravies, but they've never come out this good. I've always used oil and never butter and I think that, that makes all the difference.

I didn't use cream, as I did not have it and the gravy was just as good. I did add a little bit of whole milk though. I will definitely use this time and time again. I know it was good because my husband enjoyed it and he is picky, picky, picky!! Thanks!!

Excellent easy recipe. I didn't have the cream, added just a touch of milk and a little bit (about a teaspoon) of cornstarch. I also added a few dried parsley flakes and a tiny bit of sage. Just mainly for color and because I was serving it with a sage stuffing. Thanks for a great recipe.

This is a good, basic, well-written recipe for gravy that will appeal to all those who either have never made gravy or who aren’t confident preparing it. I used the drippings from a roasted turkey breast plus enough boxed chicken stock to make up the difference. The cream was a nice addition, something I don’t generally use. I didn’t care for the light color of the gravy, however, particularly since I was using it for sliced roast turkey, but a little dribble of Kitchen Bouquet fixed that right up.

Mmm, amazing! So good with our roast chicken and mashed potatoes. My gravy wasn't getting thick at a simmer so I increased the heat and brought it to a low boil whisking constantly (this is how my mom does it) until it was thick to my liking, then turned off the heat and added the cream, s/p and cayenne. Thanks so much for the recipe:)

This is similar to the old Fanny Farmer chicken pot pie gravy recipe. I add a touch of poultry seasoning to mine and a dash of nutmeg. I then pour it over roughly cubed chicken, drained can of LeSeur peas, carmelized onion pieces and well-cooked sliced carrots. A topping of Bisquick biscuits finishes it off, with a sprinkling of grated parmesan cheese over the biscuits. There usually aren't any leftovers!

I made this 2 times already this week. First with leftover chicken from a roast, I used chicken broth instead of drippings & cut the recipe in half. We all loved it & honestly I was never a gravy fan. Today I roasted a 4lb. pork shoulder. I coated the roast with a can of cream of mushroom soup. When cooking was complete the juices measured 2 cups, then Iadded 2 cups of water. I took the advise & cooked the roux for the 12 minutes. OMG, I normally would have eaten the pork plain, it was juicy & so tasty but I ate each bite dipped in Chef John's gravy! Yummy

Perfect gravy! Super easy to make and no lumps. I added some dried thyme to the roux and a couple drops of Worcestershire sauce at the end (a tip from one of Chef John's other recipes). Make sure you sample as you go and add salt if it's tasting too "chicken broth-y."

This is a very good base recipe, and as CF says, you can dress it up with flavorings that you like. Here is what I did, and the result was so delicious, and best of all, I made it two days before Thanksgiving, then just reheated on medium heat for about 30 minutes, stirring often, then let it sit on low until dinner, about 30 more. 

So in a nutshell, start reheating about one hour before dinnertime. Watch the video for technique. It is so easy. And I used an ordinary carton of Campbell chicken broth, regular salt, so definitely do NOT add any salt at all to the sauce.

After stirring in the broth and bringing that to a boil, I cooked gently for about 10 minutes. That gets the flour taste out. After that I stirred in 1/4 cup marsala wine, 1/2 tsp poultry seasoning and 1/4 white pepper. Cook that for about 2 minutes then stir in the cream and do not boil again. Let it cool to room temp, then keep in fridge. Reheat per instructions above. Don't boil it when you reheat, as the cream could then separate. I had no issues. The gravy is good. 

You can double everything, which I do if I am cooking for more than 8. This is so, so easy, and I would not dream of making this right before Thanksgiving dinner, with the stress of using turkey drippings, etc. Not for me. Make this a few days ahead and enjoy a stress-free T-giving dinner.

This was great! Very good for a base recipe, but I had to add some extra spices for more flavor. I added cooked, cubed chicken breast and served over mashed potatoes, with homemade biscuits on the side. Came out wonderful, and the whole family LOVED this gravy. Definitely saving this one (:
This gravy was really good! I followed the recipe as written. Easy instructions.

I made the gravy for chicken and biscuits and it was delicious! After the gravy was done, I added cooked shredded chicken and served it over baking powder biscuits. As suggested in some of the other reviews, I added 1/4 teaspoon of garlic powder along with the other seasonings. This recipe is definitely a keeper and I will be making it again!
I've made it twice and it's delicious. Second time didn't have white pepper. I used regular black pepper and it was just as good. Very easy recipe to read. Thank you very much

This was a nice recipe, but I prefer my gravy to be a little richer. In the future I’d add garlic (garlic and/or onion powder are usually necessary for me in a gravy) and some chicken bouillon. It was nice and creamy, but just a little light on flavor in my opinion.
I started out halving the recipe since there are only two of us at dinner.Followed the recipe to the letter, even though the times seemed a little long. Best darned chicken gravy I have ever had!
Used this in the Chicken Dijon Chicken recipe also on this site. I would make it again using more of the spices listed.
